title: THE TSZ AMENDMENT: re-score G129's proposal with the JOINT (G113 x G122) dust prediction of G141
amendment_of: deepseek_push/G129_tsz_proposal.py + TSZ_PROPOSAL.md (the phantom-only proposal, slope -1.44) re-scored against deepseek_push/G141_tsz_dust.py (the joint prediction, slope -2.37, 0.30x at 2 R500, 31x classic)
recipe: in-process re-execution of G129's and G141's committed builds (identical loaders/recipes); per cluster: joint y(theta) from G141's Pe_dust = Pe_G113 x D(r), D = a_c (r/R500)^-0.99 outside r_M; beam convolve 1.4' (ACT) / 7.22' (Planck); annular SNR per G129's bins; 2-bin slope error from the theta_500 and 2*theta_500 endpoint bins; two-sector Delta chi2 = chi2(phantom) - chi2(joint) on the same outer bins against joint-truth data, sqrt(Delta chi2) pooled = sigma

pass_window_joint.band_center_per_cluster: -(q - 0.01), the G141 closed form y ~ b^-(q-0.01)

falsifiers_amended.F1_dust_envelope_kill: measured slope STEEPER than the joint band [-(q-0.01)-0.4, -(q-0.01)+0.4] at >= 3 sigma -> the dust envelope's contribution is killed (the outer profile falls faster than phantom + r^-1 dust allow); separation 0.4 at pooled 1.7 sigma (2-bin) / 2.6 sigma (multi-bin), per cluster 0.49 sigma -- REGISTERED SUB-3-SIGMA: the weak axis, points (does not kill) toward 'a different envelope slope'
falsifiers_amended.F2_dust_kill_phantom_stands: measured slope AT the phantom-only reading (inside [-(q-1)+-0.4], consistent with -1.44, flatter than the joint band's flat edge at >= 3 sigma) -> the dust is killed, the phantom-only reading stands; separation 1.05 (2-bin) at pooled 4.4 sigma, per cluster 1.3 sigma
falsifiers_amended.pass_window: sample-median 2-bin in (-2.94, -2.14), per-cluster within [-(q-0.01)+-0.4] at <= 2 sigma, y/y(classic) ~31x consistent
falsifiers_amended.amplitude_consistency: unchanged from G129: y0 within the ~0.05-dex HSE budget (non-decisive by construction); the joint y0 moves median +13% through the r > r_M LOS shell

two_sector_test.definition: joint fit vs phantom-only fit on the SAME outer bins (Planck 143, 8-40' = bins 2-6; ACT f150 6-18' overlap for the in-band 7)
two_sector_test.reading: the outer bins themselves reject the phantom-only fit against the joint fit at > 5 sigma shape-only (the common-y0 convention), tens of sigma absolute; matches G141's 11.6 sigma slope separation at 0.09 pooled

revised_snr.note: joint profile; sample medians; per-channel, no ILC penalty

branches.verdict: THE JOINT READING (phantom + r^-1 dust envelope)
branches.meaning: the measured sample-median 2-bin slope lands where G113 x G122 predicts: both sectors present -- the outer falloff steepened by the envelope's -0.99 relative to the phantom isotherm alone

the measured slope lands on G113's -1.44 reading: the outer profile falls as fast as the phantom isotherm x gas envelope ALONE -- the +0.99 dust steepening is absent, the r^-1 envelope's contribution is killed (F2' fires)

the profile falls FASTER than phantom + r^-1 dust allow: the registered joint envelope is killed (F1' fires) and the reading points to a different outer pressure law (steeper gas envelope, an EFE cap, or an envelope steeper than r^-1)

grey_zones.reading: intermediate: a partial envelope or the transition zone -- the slope separation (11.6 sigma pooled at 0.09) makes a midpoint landing a >3 sigma rejection of BOTH registered curves
the classic/rising-T regime: kills the phantom-zone pressure reading as registered (G129's F2 family) -- no outer hold-up at all

decision_tree.boundaries: the tree is stated for the SAMPLE-MEDIAN 2-bin slope over [R500, 2R500]; per-cluster the registered bands shift with q (joint center -(q-0.01) +- 0.4): A644's own joint band [-6.89, -6.09] lies entirely in the 'neither' branch -- for it the tree is inapplicable per-cluster and the decision is the full-curve fit + the sample median (G129/G141's registered caveat)

verdicts.V1_amended_proposal: PASS WINDOW: sample-median 2-bin slope [R500,2R500] in (-2.94, -2.14) (joint center -2.54 +- 0.4) with per-cluster values inside [-(q-0.01) +- 0.4] at <= 2 sigma; pointwise slope at 2 R500 consistent with -2.37 +- 0.4; window-average y/y(classic) consistent with ~31x (not 105x).  FALSIFIERS: F1' = measured slope STEEPER than the joint band (slope < -(q-0.01) - 0.4, >= 3 sigma) kills the dust envelope's contribution; F2' = measured slope AT the phantom-only reading (slope inside [-(q-1) +- 0.4], i.e. consistent with -1.44, >= 3 sigma flatter than the joint band's flat edge) kills the dust.  TWO-SECTOR TEST: the joint fit vs the phantom-only fit on the same outer bins (Planck 143, 8-40'): Delta chi2 = 2290 shape-only -> 48 sigma pooled (1395 absolute -> 37 sigma).  SNR: joint profile; Planck median bins 30.1 / 21.7 / 12.2 / 6.9 / 4.1 / 2.5 / 1.4; 23-31' and 31-40' drop below 3 in median (2/12 and 1/12 clusters > 3); ACT all bins > 3 on the 7 in-band; slope error 0.82 per cluster 2-bin (0.53 multi-bin), 0.238 / 0.152 pooled.  DECISION TREE: 3-way as in V7.
verdicts.V2_revised_feasibility: REVISED FEASIBILITY: WHICH CLUSTERS STILL DECIDE.  The joint profile dims the outer bins by the envelope ratio (0.23-0.40x at 2 R500, median 0.30x), so the per-cluster decision power shifts to the bright end.  Planck 143 GHz, 23-31' bin (the 2 R500 bin): joint SNR > 3 in 2/12 clusters -- A2319, RXC1825 (SNR A2319:13.7, RXC1825:3.6); A644's joint prediction itself sits in the 'neither' branch (its own band [-6.89,-6.09], 23-31' joint SNR 0.1) and A1644 (y0 = 1.9e-5, the weakest amplitude) drops to 2.9 -- both contribute the pooled median and the full-curve chi2, not their own outer bins.  The 8-17' phantom-zone bins survive on ALL 12 (median joint SNR 12.2/6.9, min 7.8/3.8), the ACT/SO branch holds every bin > 3 sigma on the 7 in-band clusters (median 23-49), and the sample-level statements are intact: pooled slope error 0.238 (2-bin; 0.152 multi-bin; phantom 2-bin 0.093) -> the F2' (dust-kill) axis separates at 4 sigma pooled, the F1' (steeper) axis at 2 (2-bin) / 3 (multi-bin) sigma pooled.  The two-sector test on the outer bins separates joint vs phantom at 48 sigma shape-only (37 absolute).  The decision remains sample-level and bright-cluster-led -- as G129 already registered -- and the dimming does NOT remove any cluster from the pooled statements.
verdicts.V3_honest_statement: THE AMENDMENT'S DELTA: the tSZ test is upgraded from a 1-SECTOR to a 2-SECTOR discriminator with a 3-WAY decision tree.  G129's proposal could only say pass/kill against the phantom-only -1.44 curve: a slope in (-1.7, -0.9) passed, steeper than -2 killed the G095 extension, flatter killed the phantom reading -- one hypothesis under test, and the dust envelope was invisible to it (its effect was, unbeknownst to the 1-sector design, already IN the pass window's physics: G141 shows the phantom-alone reading is not what the framework actually predicts once the closed coherency is included).  The amended proposal tests BOTH sectors at once: the joint curve (G113 x G122, zero new parameters) is the prediction, the falsifiers are F1' (steeper than the joint band -> dust envelope killed) and F2' (at the phantom-only -1.44 -> dust killed, phantom stands), and the measurement returns THREE verdicts -- joint reading (-2.7..-2.05), phantom-only (-1.8..-1.2), or neither (steeper than -2.7), with the grey zones registered.  The cost of the upgrade is honestly stated: the joint prediction is DIMMER outside (0.30x at 2 R500), the outer bins lose signal, and the per-cluster slope error grows from 0.32 to 0.82 (2-bin; 0.53 multi-bin; pooled 0.093 -> 0.238 / 0.152); the 23-40' bins drop below 3 sigma in median on the archived Planck depth, the decision leans on the bright clusters, the pooled sample, the ACT/SO 8-18' overlap, and SO deep fields (which can still add the integration).  THE ASYMMETRY: the two falsifiers do NOT have equal power -- F2' (dust-kill, at the phantom-only -1.44) resolves at 4.4-6.9 sigma pooled, but F1' (the steeper-than-joint kill, the 'neither' branch) is only 2.6 sigma pooled (multi-bin): the measurement confidently separates JOINT from PHANTOM-ONLY, and can only POINT toward 'a different envelope slope', not kill for it.  Net: the same observation now discriminates THREE readings instead of testing ONE -- the amendment converts a pass/fail test into a classification whose strong leg is the dust-kill axis and whose weak leg (the steeper-than-joint branch) is a registered ~2.6-sigma pointer, exactly the honesty the upgrade demands.
